_comment: Frond globals contract, governed by ADR-0085 (aligns Python/PHP/Ruby to Node under ADR-0004).
A bare zero-argument callable global is invoked and its RETURN VALUE is used for both
{{ g }} output and {% if g %} conditions. Explicit g() still works and never double-calls.
A non-callable global is unchanged, a global that returns a callable is called once, and an
unregistered nope() is falsy rather than an error.
The same seven pure in-memory cases run in all four frameworks without mocks: the closures are
real and each framework renders real template source. Node is the reference; its suite is a guard.

invariants.rule: A bare reference to a zero-argument callable global is invoked; its return value is used for {{ g }} output and {% if g %} truthiness.
invariants.why: Node auto-calls a bare zero-argument callable global (ADR-0004); Python/PHP/Ruby stored the callable, so {% if admin_only %} was always truthy (#90).
cases: zero arg global closure returning false is falsy in if
zero arg global closure returning true is truthy in if
zero arg global closure prints its return value

invariants.rule: g() keeps working and calls the global exactly once through the function-call path.
invariants.why: Auto-calling a bare reference must not break the explicit call form, and must not combine with it into a double call.

invariants.rule: A non-callable global (string/number/bool) is used as-is; only callables are affected.
invariants.why: The change is scoped to callable globals and must not touch plain values.

invariants.rule: A global that returns a callable is called once, yielding the inner callable; the inner callable is not then called.
invariants.why: Calling once is the contract; a bare reference must not chain into a second call of the returned value.
cases: global returning a callable is not double called

invariants.rule: An unregistered nope() resolves to a falsy/empty value rather than raising.
invariants.why: Existing behaviour in all four; pinned so it stays consistent alongside the auto-call rule.
